communications.subject: South Dakota Open Records Law Request: Deaths-in-custody (South Dakota Department of Public Safety)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the South Dakota Open Records Law, I hereby request the following records:

The database or records of all Illinois law enforcement agencies deaths-in-custody up to the date this request is ultimately fulfilled, including all deaths-in-custody reported pursuant both Illinois state legislation (730 ILCS 210/3-5) and federal legislation (34 U.S.C. § 60105), as well as all data dictionaries, database scheme documentation or other documentation on the collection and organizatin of the data. 

I request these records in their native digital formats and not in formats that degrade the accessibility of the records, such as tabular data converted to PDF or Word files. If converting the native digital format to another high-fidelity format, such as CSV or Excel, please take care not to introduce formatting inconsistencies or errors, which can occur in the conversion process (for example, encoding errors or the inclusion of internal unescaped quotation marks in CSV files). Should the records above represent certain values as numeric codes or abbreviations that are not self-explanatory, we additionally request all records necessary to interpret those codes and abbreviations.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Dillon Bergin

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: USAID Ebola audits
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

- All the drafts or final reports of audits and/or investigations and/or desk reviews undertaken by the Office of the Inspector General on the response to the 10th, 11th and/or 12th Ebola epidemics in the Democratic Republic of Congo. The timeframe is 14 April 2020 to today. This includes any updates regarding complaint 19-0852 and 20-0502 inter alia.
- All reports of the visit  by a delegation of U.S. officials to the Democratic Republic of Congo to assess the response to the outbreak. The timeframe is 14 April 2020 until today-

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Emmanuel Freudenthal

communications.subject: FOIA processing delays due to COVID-19 Re: Freedom of Information Act Request: USAID Ebola audits
communications.communication:
USAID has implemented maximum telework to promote social distancing during the COVID-19 pandemic.  Priorities in many of our operating units have shifted, thus impacting processing response times. Please note that USAID is unable to conduct a search for physical records while teleworking.  As a result, all search requests will be limited to electronic records, unless you notify us that you want your request to remain open until USAID employees have physical access to their workspaces. We appreciate your understanding during this time.  If you have any questions, please email us at foia@usaid.gov .  Thank you. 

--

October 21, 2021 RE:  USAID FOIA No. F-00026-22 (Acknowledgment Letter) Dear Mr. Freudenthal: Thank you for your letter dated October 21, 2021, requesting information pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act (FOIA), 5 U.S.C. §  552.  The tracking number for your request is F-00026-22.  Please use this number when corresponding with our office. At this time, we are in the process of perfecting your request.  A perfected request for records reasonably describes such records and is made in accordance with published rules stating the time, place, fees (if any) and procedures to be followed.  This process includes reviewing the request for clarity and fee category determination and related commitment to pay, if applicable. Once your request is perfected, you will be notified of the FOIA Specialist assigned to process your case.  If you have questions, please contact us at .  Please cite the above-referenced number when corresponding with our office. (mailto:foia@usaid.gov) foia@usaid.gov Thank you. Sincerely, Diamond Johnson

communications.subject: USAID FOIA REQUEST No. F-00026-22 (FOIA Specialist Assignment Email)
communications.communication:
October 21, 2021 RE:  USAID FOIA No. F-00026-22 (FOIA Specialist Assignment Email) Dear Mr. Freudenthal: This acknowledges receipt of your October 21, 2021, Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) request to the United States Agency for International Development (USAID).  Specifically, you requested records concerning: All the drafts or final reports of audits and/or investigations and/or desk reviews undertaken by the Office of the Inspector General on the response to the 10th, 11th and/or 12th Ebola epidemics in the Democratic Republic of Congo. The timeframe is 14 April 2020 to today. This includes any updates regarding complaint 19-0852 and 20-0502 inter alia.- All reports of the visit by a delegation of U.S. officials to the Democratic Republic of Congo to assess the response to the outbreak. The timeframe is 14 April 2020 until today-(Date Range for Record Search: From 4/14/2020 To 10/21/2021). 
Fee 
The FOIA provides that fees should be waived or reduced if disclosure of the information is in the public interest because it is likely to contribute significantly to public understanding of the operations and activities of the government and is not primarily in the commercial interest of the requester.  As a member of the media, the only applicable fee is duplication.  Duplication is $0.10 per page, but the first 100 pages are free. Since the only applicable fee is duplication, and USAID routinely furnishes responsive records to FOIA requesters in electronic format, it's most likely there will be no duplication fees to assess. 
FOIA Specialist 
Your request has been assigned to Theresa Morris, Senior FOIA Specialist.  You may contact Theresa Morris by email at thmorris@usaid.gov or by phone on 202-921-5003.  Please reference the tracking number cited above in any future correspondence. 
Extending the FOIA’s Time Limits due to Unusual Circumstances The FOIA provides that an agency  may extend its time limits when “unusual circumstances” occur in the processing of a request. See 5 U.S.C. § 552(a)(6)(B)(i) (2016).  Those “unusual circumstances” are set forth in the statute, 5 U.S.C § 552(a)(6)(B)(iii), and are described as: 1) The need to search for records from field facilities or other locations separate from the office processing the request; 2) The need to search, collect and examine voluminous records; and 3) The need for consultation with another agency. Based upon the records you have requested, we have determined that one or more unusual circumstances will occur during the processing of your request.  Accordingly, your response time-limit has been extended beyond the 20 days required by statute; therefore, 10 additional processing days have been added to your request. To mitigate this action, you may limit the scope of the request so that it can be processed more quickly or to arrange an alternative time to respond. If you have any questions or wish to discuss reformulation or an alternative time frame for the processing of your request, you may contact the assigned FOIA Specialist noted above. You may also contact USAID’s FOIA Public Liaison, Christopher Colbow, at foia@usaid.gov. (mailto:foia@usaid.gov) 

Additionally, you may contact the Office of Government Information Services (OGIS) at the National Archives and Records Administration to inquire about the FOIA mediation services offered: Office of Government Information Services National Archives and Records Administration 8601 Adelphi Road-OGIS, College Park, Maryland 20740-6001 E-mail: ogis@nara.gov Telephone: 202-741-5770; Toll Free: 1-877-684-6448 Fax: 202-741-5769 Thank you for your interest in USAID. Sincerely, Diamond Johnson 
FOIA Specialist 
Bureau for Management 
Office of Management Services 
Information and Records Division

communications.subject: USAID FOIA Email Receipt RE: Freedom of Information Act Request #F-00026-22
communications.communication:
Greetings - 

Thank you for contacting the USAID FOIA office. We have received your request and will respond within 48 hours. 

Kindly be informed of the following: 

Requesting records containing personally identifiable information (PII): 
1st Party Request: 
If you are requesting records about yourself, we must verify your identity prior to initiating a search for records. Please complete and return t he AID form 507-1, Certification of Identity, located here: https://www.usaid.gov/forms/aid-507-1. Please submit the completed form in addition to the source documents outlined in section 2 encrypted via (https://www.usaid.gov/forms/aid-507-1) foia@usaid.gov, accompanied by a password in a separate email. (mailto:foia@usaid.gov) 
3rd Party Request: 
If you are requesting records concerning another individual on their behalf, you must provide a statement from that individual verifying their identity. Please have the subject of the request complete sections 1 and 2 of the AID form 507-1, Certification of Identity, located here: https://www.usaid.gov/forms/aid-507-1. As the 3rd party requester, please complete section 3. Send the completed form and source documents outlined in section 2 encrypted via (https://www.usaid.gov/forms/aid-507-1) foia@usaid.gov, accompanied by a password, prior initiating a search for records. (mailto:foia@usaid.gov) 
Requesting acquisition (contracts, etc.) and assistance (grants, cooperative agreements, etc.) awards: 

We receive many requests for procurement documents: solicitations, proposals, and contracts. Sometimes our requesters only provide us with the solicitation number. If possible, when you are requesting winning proposals, please provide the following additional information: the office that issued the solicitation, the title of the solicitation, the name of the successful bidder, and the number of the resulting award. For procurement documents, please provide the award number, office that issued the award, program name, and geographic location. 

Thank you, 

USAID FOIA Team 

-- 
V/r, FOIA Specialist US AID - US Agency for International Development FOIA Office Bureau for Management, Office of Management Services, Information and Records Division (M/MS/IRD) | foia@USAID.gov

communications.communication:
Dear Sir/Maam,

"On September 18, 2025, USAID sent you a letter pursuant to its “Still Interested” notice published in the Federal Register on September 16, 2025. The letter asked you to confirm whether you wished for USAID to continue processing your FOIA request and provided a response deadline of October 31, 2025.

Because we did not receive a response from you by the October 31, 2025, deadline, your FOIA request has been administratively closed under the “Still Interested” notice procedure.

If you wish USAID to reopen your request, you may reply to this email confirming that you remain interested. Please do this within five business days.  Once we have your confirmation, we will reopen and resume processing the request.

If we do not receive a reply, no further action will be taken.

Please feel free to contact us with any questions.

V/r, 
FOIA Specialist
USAID - US Agency for International Development FOIA Office
Bureau for Management, Office of Management Services, Information and Records Division (M/MS/IRD) | foia@USAID.gov"

communications.communication:

I am still interested, I had have received your letter of 18th September. Could you update me on the status of this request?

Since September 2025, I have sent you several reminders (including on 29 October 2025 and several other times). You did not respond until 29th December 2025.

On September 29, 2025, in response to an email requesting an update, you had replied:
"Hi Emmanuel,

Thanks for your continued patience. USAID currently has a limited capacity
to respond to FOIA requests.

We will work diligently to respond to your request as soon as possible.

We will reach back out when we have an update.

Respectfully,

Derwin"

This request dates back to 2021 and I would like to receive the documents that I've requested as soon as possible. Could you provide me with an estimated date of completion?

Best regards,
Emmanuel

communications.subject: Oregon Public Records Law Request: EMAILS REGARDING BEND POLICE
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Oregon Public Records Law, I hereby request the following records:

Specifically, I am requesting the following emails generated or received between January 1, 2024, and the date this request is processed: Copies of all formal and informal comments or complaints,  filed by members of the public or city employees regarding the conduct, policies, or actions of the City of Bend Police Department.  Copies of the 96 emails categorized under the "Police" topic sent to the City Council across the 2024, 2025, and 2026 calendar years dashboard.   

I request a full waiver of all fees associated with fulfilling this request. As a representative of the independent news outlet StateCreated.net, I am requesting this information for news-gathering and publication purposes. The disclosure of these records is in the public interest because it will significantly contribute to public understanding of local law enforcement operations, accountability mechanisms, and community relations.If this request is denied in whole or in part, please justify all deletions or redactions by reference to specific exemptions in the public records law. If portions of these records are exempt, please redact the exempt portions and release the remainder of the records.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days.

Sincerely,

Tristann Harrison

communications.subject: Iowa Open Records Law Request: Consulate emails with AG (Office of the Attorney General - Iowa)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Iowa Open Records Law, I hereby request the following records:

1. Emails, together with attachments, exchanged between May 1, 2022 and the date this request is received, between any employee or official of the Office of the Attorney General and any email address ending in "gov.il." The senders and recipients are identified above; the subject matter is communications between the Office and the government of Israel; the timeframe is stated above.

2. Records sufficient to show the search conducted for paragraph 1, including the accounts or custodians searched, the search terms or queries used, and the number of responsive items or hits located in each account.

I ask to be properly classified as a media requester. I am an assistant editor at Reason Magazine who has written numerous articles on topics of public interest, and I am requesting these documents in an editorial capacity. Please contact me if you have any questions about my media status. If applicable, I request a waiver of all fees associated with this request.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Matthew Petti

Good Day, 

Your Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) request of March 8, 2026 has been received by the Navy Personnel Command (NPC).  This command received your request on April 1, 2026. Your FOIA request number is 2026-NavyFOIA-006383 and your FOIA correspondence file number is 6NPC0486. 

Due to the government furlough that occurred from 1 October 2025 to 12 November 2025, the Department of the Navy was legally required to suspend all non-excepted operations, including the processing of Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) requests. During this period, FOIA personnel were prohibited from performing their duties, which resulted in unavoidable delays and a temporary halt in responding to pending inquiries. In addition, FOIA analysts who were furloughed lost access to the online Navy FOIA tracking system, Secure Release, until 10 December 2025. Now that normal operations have resumed, the FOIA Office is working diligently to address the backlog created by the furlough, and the holidays and is committed to processing requests as efficiently and transparently as possible. We appreciate the your patience and understanding during this interruption in service. 

The records you seek require a search in and/or consultation with another office, and so your request falls within the "unusual circumstances" See 5 U.S.C. § 552 (a)(6)(B)(i)-(iii).  Because of these unusual circumstances, we may need to extend the time limit to respond to your request beyond the twenty days provided by the statute.  For your information, we use multiple tracks to process requests, but within the tracks we working an agile manner.  The time needed to complete our work on your request will necessarily depend on a variety of factors, including the complexity of a records search, the volume and complexity of any material located, and the order of receipt of your request.  At this time we have assigned your request to the complex track.  Any decision with regard to the application of fees will be made only after we determine whether fees will be implicated for this request.

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: FTC v. Greystar settlement payment
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

Agency emails and attachments related to payment of the settlement in Federal Trade Commission vs. Greystar, which was announced on Dec. 2, 2025, and where payment was due January 3, 2026. 

To be more specifics, I am interested in:
Documentation showing that the $23m payment due January 2 was received, the date on which it was received, and the amount received;
Any emails discussing the logistics or terms of that payment;
Any emails discussing logistics or timeline for paying restitution to consumers.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Tracie McMillan

communications.subject: RE: Freedom of Information Act Request #FOIA-2026-00598
communications.communication:
Hello,

I'm following up on a request sent in March re: the FTC settlement with Greystar. 

THe agency response indicates a misreading of the request.

Your agency wrote, "seeking the following records within the date range for record search from December 2, 2025 to January 3, 2026."

I am seeking any and all records related to events that should have been bookkended by those dates: Greystar's payment of its settlement amount, and restitution paid to tenants. This should include all records to date since December 2, 2025.

Please let me know if you need any additional clarification?

Thank you!
take care,
Tracie McMillan
Independent Journalist / The Guardian US

communications.subject: RE: Freedom of Information Act Request #FOIA-2026-00598
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern, 

On March 25, 2026, I submitted the below request under the Freedom of Information Act. The agency acknowledged receipt of this request and assigned it tracking number FOIA-2026-00598 on March 25, 2026. 

I was told by the agency that, due to the government shut down from February 14 to April 30, 2026, it would take approximately sixty to seventy-five business days from April 10, 2026 to complete this request. That would put the due date for a response at no later than July 29, 2026.

I have sent follow ups on May 25, June 24, July 24, August 24th, and September 23, 2026, and as of this writing, the request has not been given any substantive response. 

Since more than two months have elapsed since the deadline the FTC gave itself, with no substantive determination, I am appealing the constructive denial of my request, and asking the agency to respond to my request. 

Under the Freedom of Information Act, the agency is required to either provide the document requested or outline clear reasons that they are exempt from doing so. 

Best,
Tracie McMillan

communications.subject: Massachusetts Public Records Law Request: Police PROTECT Act Compliance Sept-Oct 2026 (Attleboro Police Department)
communications.communication:
Dear Record Access Officer:

This is a request under the Massachusetts Public Records Law (M. G. L. Chapter 66, Section 10). I am requesting the following records:

1.    All municipal or police department policies, ordinances, or resolutions currently in effect regarding communication and information sharing between departmental employees and federal agents/agencies within the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) or the U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS), including but not limited to the U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE). The records request includes, but is not limited to, policies regarding:

             A. Fingerprint and other data sharing;
             B. Compliance with federal immigration enforcement efforts, including guidance or policies concerning when communication with ICE officers is allowed. This includes how and under what circumstances to respond to ICE detainer requests or when and how department employees can provide a federal immigration authority with nonpublic personal information, custody status, or advance notice of a person’s release from pretrial detention or upcoming court appearances;
             C. Any other records that indicate changes in policy or practice as a result of the passage of the Massachusetts PROTECT Act in August 2026.

 2.  All departmental and municipal policies, guidance, memos or other records concerning the use of local resources for federal civil immigration enforcement. This includes policies, requests or responses to requests for the use of municipal parking lots, police station interior or exterior areas for immigration enforcement, staging, or the transfer of custody.

3.    Any records of email, text, or phone conversations between department employees and federal DHS employees working at ICE made from September 4, 2026 until October 31, 2026 (or the date responsive records are collected for review if prior to October 31, 2026), including but not limited to email sent to any “@ice.dhs.gov” email address. This request includes any call logs or transcripts of calls.

For each request, I am not seeking identifying information of community members, and I will accept anonymized or redacted data as necessary to protect the identity of the public. Redaction of names of municipal, state, or federal government employees is not necessary.

Pursuant to 950 CMR 32.07(2)(k), I request that your agency waive fees given that these records are in the public interest and I am not requesting this for commercial interests. In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. The Public Records Law requires a written response within 10 business days. If you cannot comply with my request, you are statutorily required to provide an explanation in writing.

Sincerely,

Joshua Dankoff
Director of Strategic Initaitives
Citizens for Juvenile Justice
joshuadankoff@cfjj.org
(submitted via muckrock)

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: FBI: Joseph Ogden Dowdy
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

Any bureau documents related to Joseph Ogden Dowdy. Dowdy (born September 24th 1949 in Hudson, Colorado - died January 17th 2008 in Salt Lake City, Utah) had an extensive criminal record. Dowdy was found guilty in federal court of the "illegal transportation of wildlife in interstate commerce" and was sentenced to time in federal prison. 

A copy of his obituary should be attached to this request and another can be found here: https://www.serenicare.com/obituaries/joseph-dowdy

DOWDY's extensive criminal record has been discussed in blog posts online: https://lostnfoundblogs.com/f/paul-hibbard-the-marvins---absent-anonymous

This is a request for records about JOSEPH OGDEN DOWDY from any and all FBI offices, including HQ, field offices, legal attaches, and facilities that maintain records under the FBI’s control. Please conduct a search for any records on DOWDY held by the Salt Lake City, Denver, Cheyenne, Casper, Lander or Albuquerque field offices. DOWDY was a long time resident of both New Mexico and Wyoming. According to a blog post I just read, it is important that I state the following: "As you know, your agency is required to search the records stored at NARA’s Washington Records Center in Suitland, MD, but still technically under your agency’s control. For more information see 36 CFR 1250.8" Please also conduct a physical search of records at NARA's Washington Records Center in Suitland, for any records or documents related to JOSEPH OGDEN DOWDY. 

Please include all potentially responsive materials, including but not limited to all communications, reports, inquiries, investigations, photographs, audio files, video files, memos, directives, etc. Please include all materials found in other subject files and all materials associated with any potentially-related names and any other known aliases, nicknames, code names, or any other identifying pseudonyms or references utilized by this agency. Please consult the Central Records System and records, the Electronic Surveillance (ELSUR) Data Management System and records, Microphone Surveillance (MISUR) records, Physical Surveillance (FISUR) records, Technical Surveillance (TESUR) records, and all available cross-reference indices, databases, and records, in addition to any other locations containing potentially-responsive materials related to JOSEPH OGDEN DOWDY.

If the bureau cannot fulfill certain parts of this request or certain portions must be redacted please provide any reasonable segregable portion of a requested record after removing or redacting those portions claimed to be exempt, explain in writing the justification for redacting the record, indicate the extent of any redactions on the portion of the record which is made available or published and where technically feasible indicate on the redacted portion itself the specific exemption(s) claimed.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Robert Delaware

As posted on the Montana Board of Pardons and Parole Website at the following location: https://bopp.mt.gov/Feedback

The Montana Constitution (Art. II, sec. 9<https://leg.mt.gov/bills/mca/title_0000/article_0020/part_0010/section_0090/0000-0020-0010-0090.html>) affords the public the right to examine documents of all public bodies or agencies of the State of Montana. These requests are also known as “right to know,” “public information,” “public record,” “PIR,” but not FOIA. Freedom of Information Act is a federal right-to-know law that does not apply or control the retention or release of state records.

The Office of Public Information Requests (OPIR) was established to create a more straightforward and consistent process for the Montanans to request state records. In the State’s response to public record requests, the agencies provide consistency in the production, cost, and process of providing public records. communications.subject: North Carolina Public Records Law Request: Jail Booking Log / Arrest Register (Jan 2025-Present)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the North Carolina Public Records Law, I hereby request the following records:

To the Custodian of Records, Wake County Sheriff's Office:

Under the North Carolina Public Records Act, N.C.G.S. Section 132-1 et seq., I request the following existing records, in the public interest and not for any commercial purpose.

I request the facility's daily jail booking log (booking register / arrest blotter) for every individual booked into the Wake County Detention Center from January 1, 2025 to the present. For each booking, I request the existing fields your jail-management system already records:

1. Booking or system number;
2. Name;
3. Date and time of booking;
4. Date of release;
5. The charge(s) or hold(s) associated with the booking, as recorded in the charges field;
6. Arresting or committing agency;
7. Warrant or reference number.

This is the facility's routine booking log -- ordinary public booking information -- and I request it in the existing electronic format your jail-management system exports (a spreadsheet, CSV, or delimited file is preferred; I do not require a formatted report). N.C.G.S. Section 132-6.2 provides that public records maintained in electronic form shall be made available in electronic form. Producing an export or query of data already maintained in your system is retrieval of an existing record, not the creation of a new one.

This request is not a duplicate of Records Request No. 26-3175, which concerned a narrower subject and was closed without production of any booking log; this request seeks the Office's general booking log for all bookings in the period, a different and broader record. The booking log is the Office's own jail record and the Office is its custodian. N.C.G.S. Section 132-6.2 provides that public records maintained in electronic form shall be made available in that form, and an agency may not decline to produce them because responding requires retrieving data from a database. I am requesting the existing booking data for all bookings in the period, in any export format your system supports.

As a public-interest, non-commercial request, I ask for a fee waiver or reduction; if a fee applies, please provide an itemized written estimate before incurring any cost, and I will respond promptly, including by narrowing the date range if that helps. If any portion is withheld, please state in writing the specific legal basis as N.C.G.S. Section 132-6(a) requires, and please preserve all responsive records pending resolution. Thank you.

Glen Wasserstein
(929) 786-1863

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days.

Sincerely,

Glen Wasserstein

communications.subject: Government Records Access and Management Act Request: LexisNexis Community Crime Map Contributors - Initial Sweep
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Government Records Access and Management Act, I hereby request the following records:

This request is related to the Community Crime Map (CCM) and Accurint, both are products of LexisNexis. You are receiving this request because your agency has data at communitycrimemap.com. We are seeking documents about how your agency integrates with LexisNexis, and whether your agency shares RMS/CAD/JMS data with other law enforcement agencies via Accurint Virtual Crime Center (AVCC) or Public Safety Data Exchange (PSDEx). 

We are requesting:
1) Technical integration documents: Any documents, integrations instructions, tutorials, and similar documents from LexisNexis about how to connect your RMS/CAD/JMS systems to LexisNexis's systems. [Typically held by IT or records systems teams/vendors from when your agency originally integrated with LexisNexis's systems]
2) Agreements: The signed "XML Addendum", Database Interface Agreement, or similar legal agreement that dictates how your agency's data may be used and shared. [Typically held by legal or procurement departments]
3) Shared Data: An export of what data you share with CCM and other law enforcement agencies. This is often called a Data Classification Crime Results sheet. To obtain this, an account admin can click a link on the left-hand side under admin permissions called 'Data Classification Manager.' There is an Export link on the top right of the Data Classification Manager page. Depending on the LexisNexis product(s) you subscribe to, this may have a different name or location. We are looking for the list of data you share with LexisNexis, and who your share it with (CCM only, or also other law enforcement agencies?) [Only an CCM/Accurint Account Administrators can access these documents]

Finally, are you able to tell me whether your law enforcement data sharing is restricted to a local consortium of agencies, or if it's shared generally with other law enforcement agencies within the LexisNexis portal?

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Shawn Segal

I understand you'd like to charge $812 for 14 hours of work. Based on how other agencies have handled the same request, and the instructions I provided, this should take significantly less time, likely under an hour.

2) For the procurement record, I'm requesting a single document that should be quick to retrieve. LexisNexis uses nearly the same template across its customers, so here's an example to aid your search: https://www.documentcloud.org/documents/28549832-san-luis-obispo-avcc-addendum/
3) The last item is a small Excel file that an Accurint Virtual Crime Center (or Community Crime Map) admin can export in under five minutes. I've provided step-by-step instructions from another law enforcement agency showing how to locate and download it.

I'm hoping this compromise saves you time while providing transparency to the public.

If you believe the simplified request will take more than an hour, please confirm that the lowest-paid employee qualified to do the work earns $58 an hour, and provide an itemized breakdown showing each task performed, who performed it, their hourly rate, and the time spent on each. I'll also note that under Utah Code § 63G-2-203, and as the court held in Graham v. Davis County (1999 UT App 136), an agency may not charge for merely assembling documents. None of the records I'm requesting contain sensitive law enforcement information or PII, and not one of the dozens of agencies that have already produced them to me found any reason to redact them.

I'd like to resolve this directly and without creating an undue burden on your agency, while ensuring the public understands how your agency shares local police records with LexisNexis.

Thank you,
Shawn

communications.subject: Massachusetts Public Records Law Request: Massachusetts Public Records Law Request: Court Overtime Data (Boston Police Department)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Massachusetts Public Records Law, I hereby request the following records:

8/27/2026
Dear Records Custodian:

This is a public records request pursuant to Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 66, § 10A. I hereby request the following records. 

I hereby request an excel/CSV extraction containing all sworn officer overtime records for court overtime for all Boston Police Department employees from January 2020 through the date of this request. Please include the following field of information:
City of Boston Employee ID (6 digit ID)
Employee first name
Employee last name
Employee middle name
Badge Number
Rank
District/Taskforce
Assigned description
Charged description
Overtime date
Overtime code and description
Start time
End time
Worked hours
Billed hours
Amount paid

Similar productions have been made by the Boston Police Department in the past. See https://www.muckrock.com/foi/boston-3/overtime-court-data-request-171565/ (request made by Vijay Fisch 08/09/2024 and completed 9/10/2024). 

I understand that you are not required to create a new public record to comply with my request, see, e.g., ch. 66, §6A(d), however, extraction of data from a database or electronic record system does not constitute creating a new record. See Att’y Gen. v. Dist. Att’y for Plymouth Dist., 484 Mass. 260, 275 (2020) (“[W]here public records are in electronic form, . . . a public records request that requires a government entity to search its electronic database to extract requested data does not mean that the extracted data constitute the creation of a new record under the public records law.”); see also 950 Mass. Code Regs. 32.07(1)(f). 

Please produce the records in an electronically-accessible format, including for screen readers, excel, or CSV. See 950 Mass. Code. Regs. 32.04(5)(d). Files that are not accessible to screen readers include, for example, .pdf files or physical documents. 

I request fees be waived as my request is in the public interest. See ch. 66, § 10(d)(v); 950 Mass. Code Regs. 32.07(k). “All agencies and municipalities are strongly urged to waive fees associated with access to public records.” This request will contribute to the public’s understanding of the Boston Police Department and is not in my commercial interest. Namely, these records will be made available to the public on Muckrock.com and will be used to update the Boston Police Index, a long-term community collaboration aimed to enhance transparency and accountability of the Boston Police Department through meticulous data collection and analysis. Thus, disclosure of these records will significantly contribute to the public’s understanding of the Boston Police Department’s operations.

If you do not waive the fees associated with my request, please provide a written, itemized, good faith estimate and explanation of the fees prior to fulfilling my request. See 950 Mass. Code Regs. 32.0792)(b); see also ch. 66, § 10(e) (“A records access officer shall not charge a fee for a public record unless the records access officer responded to the requestor within 10 business days.”). 

If you believe any of the records I have requested are exempt from disclosure, please identify both: (1) the records, categories of records, or portions of the records you intend to withhold; and (2) the specific reasons for such withholding, including the specific exemption you are relying on. See ch. 66, § 10(b)(iv).

If necessary to comply with my request, I welcome your suggested modifications pursuant to ch. 66, § 10(b)(vii) and 950 Mass. Code Regs. 32.06(2)(g). I am available to discuss any proposed modifications at (781) 915-8324 and mmcsharr@bu.edu.

Thank you in advance for your time and attention to this matter. I look forward to receiving your response within 10 calendar days. See ch. 66, § 10(a). 

Sincerely,
Mikaela McSharry
BU SPARK!

I also request that, if appropriate, fees be waived as we believe this request is in the public interest, as suggested but not stipulated by the recommendations of the Massachusetts Supervisor of Public Records. The requested documents will be made available to the general public free of charge as part of the public information service at MuckRock.com, and is not made for commercial usage.

I expect the request to be filled in an accessible format, including for screen readers, which provide text-to-speech for persons unable to read print. Files that are not accessible to screen readers include, for example, .pdf image files as well as physical documents.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Mikaela McSharry

Pursuant to the Texas Public Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

First 40 emails [email subject line search match, or full body email search match] from email domains "@leonardocompany-us.com" and "@leonardo.com". 40 results maximum for each domain, for total of 80 maximum between the two domains. Full conversations, threads, or email exchanges please, preserving all parties, participants etc. Ensure attachments are preserved/rendered as well. Search BOTH quoted email domains in your email program to locate responsive material. Search "@leonardocompany-us.com" first before searching the second domain. Date range 1 January 2024 - Present. 
b. All invoices, bills, POs, account statements, requisitions, payment records for 1 January 2024- Present, from or to vendor "Leonardo", "Leonardo USA" for products including but not limited to "ELSAG", "SignalTrace", "ELSAG SignalTrace", "Trailer", "Plate Hunter", "Street Sentry", "ALPR", "LPR". Include all invoices from this vendor.
c. All contracts, MOUs, MSAs, agreements, license agreements, contract documents, data sharing agreements, from or to vendor "Leonardo" and "Leonardo USA", from 1 January 2024-Present.

2. Current and accurate map of Flock assets and their locations within City of Tyler. This is a map that Flock produces within its dashboard. It is a map, visual representation of where all cameras are located within an agency. Please ensure this map includes full City of Tyler boundaries. To be clear--this map should show every Flock brand camera the City of Tyler and Tyler Police Department, owns, operates, manages, leases, or utilizes. It may be necessary to adjust zoom level on this map to ensure every agency asset is visible. Easiest way to access map: Enter Flock dashboard/application, Select "Map", screenshot map or print the webpage as a PDF. I can provide further steps if necessary. 
This does not constitute new material. This data already exists within the Flock system, it merely has to be exported, just like any other piece of data. You should already have an AG ruling on this, but it has not been provided or posted here. Quoting the AG's 2026 Public Information Handbook: "A request for public information that requires a governmental body to program or manipulate existing data is not considered a request for the creation of new information." [https://www.texasattorneygeneral.gov/sites/default/files/files/divisions/open-government/PIA-Handbook-2026.pdf , PG 29, citing:  Fish v. Dallas Indep. Sch. Dist., 31 S.W.3d 678, 681-82 (Tex. App.—Eastland 2000, pet. denied); see Gov’t Code

iii. Other Police department email accounts that had contact with [PARTY 2, MEDIA], these accounts generally follow the account naming convention firstinitialLastname@tylertexas.com. Search email domain "@tylertexas.com", in your Police Department email system, including all police department accounts in the search. Please conduct search for items (i) and (ii) before searching (iii).

b. AND ONE OF THE FOLLOWING PARTICIPANTS in this category: MEDIA OUTLETS, "PARTY 2": 
i.  "KLTV" email domain "@kltv.com"; 
ii. "KETK" email domains "@ketk.com", "@nexstar.tv"; 
iii. "KYTX" domain "@cbs19.tv"

Restrict date range to 1 Jan 2026-Present for search of responsive emails. First 40 emails [email subject line search match, or full body email search match] from email domains "@leonardocompany-us.com" and "@leonardo.com". 40 results maximum for each domain, for total of 80 maximum between the two domains. Full conversations, threads, or email exchanges please, preserving all parties, participants etc. Ensure attachments are preserved/rendered as well. Search BOTH quoted email domains in your email program to locate responsive material. Search "@leonardocompany-us.com" first before searching the second domain. Date range 1 January 2024 - Present. 
b. All invoices, bills, POs, account statements, requisitions, payment records for 1 January 2024- Present, from or to vendor "Leonardo", "Leonardo USA" for products including but not limited to "ELSAG", "SignalTrace", "ELSAG SignalTrace", "Trailer", "Plate Hunter", "Street Sentry", "ALPR", "LPR". Include all invoices from this vendor. 
c. All contracts, MOUs, MSAs, agreements, license agreements, contract documents, data sharing agreements, from or to vendor "Leonardo" and "Leonardo USA", from 1 January 2024-Present. 

2. Current and accurate map of Flock assets and their locations within City of Tyler. This is a map that Flock produces within its dashboard. It is a map, visual representation of where all cameras are located within an agency. Please ensure this map includes full City of Tyler boundaries. To be clear--this map should show every Flock brand camera the City of Tyler and Tyler Police Department, owns, operates, manages, leases, or utilizes. It may be necessary to adjust zoom level on this map to ensure every agency asset is visible. Easiest way to access map: Enter Flock dashboard/application, Select "Map", screenshot map or print the webpage as a PDF. I can provide further steps if necessary. 
This does not constitute new material. This data already exists within the Flock system, it merely has to be exported, just like any other piece of data. You should already have an AG ruling on this, but it has not been provided or posted here. Quoting the AG's 2026 Public Information Handbook: "A request for public information that requires a governmental body to program or manipulate existing data is not considered a request for the creation of new information." [https://www.texasattorneygeneral.gov/sites/default/files/files/divisions/open-government/PIA-Handbook-2026.pdf , PG 29, citing: Fish v. Dallas Indep. Sch. Dist., 31 S.W.3d 678, 681-82 (Tex. App.—Eastland 2000, pet. denied); see Gov’t Code 
§ 552.231; Attorney General Opinion H-90 (1973); Open Records Decision Nos. 452 at 2-3 (1986), 87 (1975). 

3. Emails with the following parties or participants in the same email exchange or email threads "PARTY 1, TYLER POLICE" and "PARTY 2, MEDIA" (defined below), and whose email content-- the email subject line or email body text-- includes any of the following keywords or terms: "alpr", "flock", "flock safety", "lpr", "license plate", "camera": 
a. ONE OF THE FOLLOWING PARTICIPANTS in this category, TYLER PD, "PARTY 1" : 
i. Police Chief Toler, "jtoler@tylertexas.com" and any other city email accounts he exercises control or ownership of . 
ii. Office of Public Information, Andy Erbaugh, email "aerbaugh@tylertexas.com", and any other email accounts he or that department exercises control of, which are "Office of Public Information accounts". Accounts are in format "@tylertexas.com". 
iii. Other Police department email accounts that had contact with [PARTY 2, MEDIA], these accounts generally follow the account naming convention firstinitialLastname@tylertexas.com. Search email domain "@tylertexas.com", in your Police Department email system, including all police department accounts in the search. Please conduct search for items (i) and (ii) before searching (iii). 

b. AND ONE OF THE FOLLOWING PARTICIPANTS in this category: MEDIA OUTLETS, "PARTY 2": 
i. "KLTV" email domain "@kltv.com"; 
ii. "KETK" email domains "@ketk.com", "@nexstar.tv"; 
iii. "KYTX" domain "@cbs19.tv" 

Restrict date range to 1 Jan 2026-Present for search of responsive emails. Notify prior to production of emails if responsive emails exceed 100 total, in which case size of this portion of request will be reduced. Full conversations, threads, or email exchanges please, preserving all parties, participants etc. Ensure attachments are preserved/rendered, exported as well. 

4. Flock Documentation. 
a. Produce all invoices, bills, POs, account statements, payment records, requisitions from or to "Flock", "Flock Group", and "Flock Safety" for 1 January 2025 to present. Invoices are public documents and should be produced in a timely manner. 
b. List of all active "hardware", which are tangible and physical surveillance devices, and current locations. Hardware includes but is not limited to: "Falcon", "Flex", "Trailer", "Drone", "Raven" and "Condor". 

Notify in advance of any proposed redaction. Requester will not agree to any redaction until notice with valid cited reason has been provided. 

Please produce easily-releasable material as soon as possible so not to waste time. 

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes. 

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not. 

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days, as the statute requires. 

Sincerely, 

Piney Woods ALPR 

Upload documents directly: https://www.muckrock.com/respond/2415730/ 
Your request will be forwarded to the relevant City of Tyler Police Department division(s) to locate the information you seek and to determine the volume and any costs associated with satisfying your request. You will be contacted about the availability and/or provided with copies of the records in question. PLEASE NOTE: The Chapter 552 of Texas Government Code, the Public Information Act does not require a governmental body to create new information, to do legal research, or to answer questions. 
 
You can monitor the progress of your request at the link below and you'll receive an email when your request has been completed. Again, thank you for using the Public Records Center. 
City of Tyler Police Department

communications.communication:
Given your response letter the following amendments and clarifications are stipulated to stop any unneces

| Item One deals broadly with emails and invoices and other payment records from Leonardo USA. You maintain you have no emails or other records from them. To consider this portion of the request for information closed, I request that you show your work and simply conduct the email search for "@leonardocompany-us.com" and the other Leonardo email domain. Leonardo frequently solicits Law enforcement agencies with unprompted emails. East Texas Auto Theft Task Force, which Tyler PD is a core member of, received an award from Leonardo in 2019. Accordingly please provide proof of zero results. An acceptable way of doing is is conducting the search and screenshotting the results. See the following references, about East Texas Auto Theft Task Force/ Tyler PD, which give clear evidence communication should exist:

i) [Video] And The 2019 IACP/Leonardo Leadership Award Goes To... -- "For several years now, Leonardo sponsors the Leadership in the Prevention of Vehicle Crimes Award in the annual IACP Leadership Awards. Given to those who represent initiative, innovation, and excellence in law enforcement practices, the awards are a true honor for recipients and we congratulate all the winners. 

As for the IACP/Leonardo Leadership in the Prevention of Vehicle Crimes Award in particular, this award is open to agencies large and small. Entries are evaluated on initiative, use of available resources, and overall results.

With that, congratulations to the 2019 winner: East Texas Auto Theft Task Force (ETATTF).

Comprised of five participating jurisdictions, the ETATTF showed outstanding initiative in the previous fiscal year. Read more about them and the award here.

In the video below, hear from Lieutenant Kenneth Richbourg; Christopher McDonold, Director of the Vehicle Theft Prevention Council; and our own Julio Valcarcel, VP of Sales for Leonardo.  " {source: https://www.leonardocompany-us.com/lpr/blog/iacp-leadership-award-2019 }

ii) Tyler PD's website explains task force composition, "The East Texas Auto Theft Task Force is a multi-agency task force which is funded by the Texas Automobile Burglary and Theft Prevention Authority and administered by the Smith County District Attorney's Office. Its members include four law enforcement officers and one secretary from the following police agencies: Department of Public Safety, Tyler Police Department, Smith County Sheriff's Office, Rusk County Sheriff's Office and Upshur County Sheriff's Office". Website notes Tyler PD detective Jimmy Turner is the department lead for the task force. PLEASE ENSURE his name is included in the email search. If you have not already done that, please do so now. His email should be "Jturner@tylertexas.com" or other similar derivative. {source: https://www.tylerpolice.com/Administration/Investigations }. Please ensure every Tyler PD member of East Texas Auto Theft Task Force's email is searched. There should be responsive results. Additionally I proactively maintain that a solicitation email or award email regarding the award from Leonardo is not excludable given that the award was presented publicly with names of task force members, and such an email may explain the relationship that Tyler PD has with private vendors who may get public funds for contracts. Further, marketing emails don't have a public records exclusionary basis for safety, trade secrets, active investigation. 

| Item Two-- Relating to item two, "map", I note the following. It does not constitute new information per applicable AG rulings mentioned in original request. Second, I note that Smith County Sheriff released their map already, without obstruction or delay (see produced Flock map at following link, included in final document package at bottom of page: https://www.muckrock.com/foi/smith-county-2746/flock-alpr-asset-list-and-map-smith-county-sheriffs-office-216908/ ). Other departments have as well all over Texas. These cameras are not covert and are prominently visible in public locations, with no attempt at disguise. Further, department does media interviews to champion the cameras, saying that they're public and mentioning how many there are, see:  https://www.kltv.com/2026/08/13/tyler-police-chief-defends-use-license-plate-cameras-amid-privacy-concerns/ . Direct quotes below:

Chief Toler proudly explains their ostensibly public network, " “It’s not a new technology,” Toler said in an interview. “It’s just a technology that’s more prominent nowadays because the costs have come down.”

The department currently controls nine Flock cameras — seven stationary and two mobile “flex” cameras that are moved to high-crime areas to identify suspect vehicles. Toler emphasized that the vast majority of license plate readers operating in Tyler are privately owned by homeowners associations, businesses and private property owners.

He continues: "“We are in public places every day,” Toler said, comparing the license plate readers to security cameras in local businesses and residential Ring doorbells. “We don’t live in a surveillance state.”

I note that further Tyler PD's partial release of emails in this request already reveals that have no issue doing media interviews to talk about the cameras or disclose how many there are.

I also that that request LD-15123, which is your internal designation for it, for request about Leonardo emails, Flock map, and Flock invoices, as well as emails about "trailer" was never completed. You provided solicitation emails about trailer, applied for AG ruling for every other item, never shared the ruling with me, despite my multiple emails, and produced no substantive materials. See following link: https://www.muckrock.com/foi/tyler-3007/flock-alpr-signaltrace-and-surveillancetech-request-216906/#comms

I would urge you, at bare minimum, to refine the Leonardo email research, of which you have had several months to complete, and start producing invoices from Flock. You should already have a ruling on releasing invoices for Flock from previous requests, as well as the map. I would also ask that you disclose the final AG ruling from previous request, hyperlinked already, and start document production given your lack of response to emails addressed to City Attorney department.

Additionally, given the delay on item four, map of Flock camera assets, I now also request, as an amendment, that you submit to me all site surveys, site plans, right of way approvals, right of way proposals, transportation documents, or schematics relating to placement of all city of Tyler Flock cameras on city right of ways, or state road right of ways. This includes materials sent internally to City of Tyler, Tyler City Council, Tyler Transportation or Roads department, and external material sent to Texas Department of Transportation for emplacement of cameras on State Highway Right of Ways. I maintain these documents are public and approved in a public manner. TxDoT's email follows format "@txdot.gov". City of tyler's email follows format at "@tylertexas.com". 

I generally maintain that City forfeited the right to keep camera locations secret because one there are public right of way documents voted for in an open city council meeting or sent to TxDoT. And two because they did media interviews talking about the equipment, quantity of equipment, etc.

communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Connecticut Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

The database or records of all Illinois law enforcement agencies deaths-in-custody up to the date this request is ultimately fulfilled, including all deaths-in-custody reported pursuant both Illinois state legislation (730 ILCS 210/3-5) and federal legislation (34 U.S.C. § 60105), as well as all data dictionaries, database scheme documentation or other documentation on the collection and organizatin of the data. 

I request these records in their native digital formats and not in formats that degrade the accessibility of the records, such as tabular data converted to PDF or Word files. If converting the native digital format to another high-fidelity format, such as CSV or Excel, please take care not to introduce formatting inconsistencies or errors, which can occur in the conversion process (for example, encoding errors or the inclusion of internal unescaped quotation marks in CSV files). Should the records above represent certain values as numeric codes or abbreviations that are not self-explanatory, we additionally request all records necessary to interpret those codes and abbreviations.

I also request that, if possible and pursuant to Conn. Gen. Stat. § 1-212(d), fees be waived as I believe this request is in the public interest and not made for commercial gain. The requested documents will be made available to the public at MuckRock.com.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 4 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Dillon Bergin

I’m following up regarding clarification for Request #26‑929. To help us process your request efficiently, could you please help us narrow or better define its scope? As currently written, requesting all maps, records, and Industrial Siting Division (ISD) socioeconomic and environmental impact assessments for all proposed, approved, and existing wind energy projects across Albany, Goshen, Laramie, and Platte Counties encompasses a vast volume of material. Fulfilling it as-is would require well over a week (estimate) of dedicated staff research to identify, pull, and review both electronic files and physical paper records. Because this request will require significant staff time, we will need to prepare a formal cost estimate for the associated labor fees before we can begin processing. If you are able to narrow the scope, such as specifying particular project names, document types (like final ISD permit decisions or specific environmental impact sections), or a narrower timeframe, we can provide a much lower cost estimate or potentially fulfill the request without incurring labor fees. Please let us know how you would like to proceed. Thank you, and have a great day. ************************************************************************ Questions about your request? Reply to this email or sign in to contact staff at WYDEQ.

communications.subject: RE: Wyoming Public Records Act Request #26-929
communications.communication:
Thank you very much for the reply. I appreciate the opportunity to narrow my request. Would the following be suitable and more tailored?

For Platte, Goshen, Laramie and Albany Counties:

1. A map of all existing wind energy projects. Or, if that is not available, the final ISD permit decisions for all existing wind energy projects. 

2. The final ISD permit decisions for all wind energy projects approved by the Industrial Siting Board within the past three years (ie, those that are allowed to commence construction). Such permit decisions could also include projects approved more than three years ago but which have had their permits extended and therefore can still commence construction

3. Any pending permit applications under consideration by the ISD for those four counties.

Is this request more reasonable? I am, in a nutshell, trying to get a sense of how many wind energy projects do exist and could soon exist in the area. 

Once I have the names and locations of all the projects, I will then make a more tailored request for their socioeconomic analysis, if I'm unable to locate that information on my own.

Thank you very much! And I'm happy to chat over the phone about how to tailor this request. 

best

Taylor Barnes

communications.subject: New Mexico Inspection of Public Records Act Request: FOIA:Jorge Dominguez
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the New Mexico Inspection of Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

Dear Custodian of records,I am submitting this request under the Opean Records Act in my capacity as a volunteer researcher. This request is made in pursuit of transparency, accountability, and public understanding related to a specific incident involving law enforcement.Requested Records:aDashcam & Body-Worn Camera (BWC) Footage:Footage from the first two officers to arrive on the scene.Any available BWC footage documenting the arrest or interaction with the primary suspect.911 Calls & Dispatch Audio (If Available):911 audio calls related to the incident.Dispatcher audio, call logs, and CAD (Computer-Aided Dispatch) reports.Police Report & Additional Records:The full report from the primary officer.If available, the probable cause affidavit.Any photographs, incident reports, and arrest reports related to this incident.

Incident Information:The following details are provided to help locate the correct records:
Suspect Name: Jorge Dominguez
Title of Case:   Bodycam Shows Deadly Clash that Left N.M. Police K-9, Armed Suspect Dead
Date of Incident:  May 29, 2025
Date of Arrest: June 17, 2025
City & State:Albuquerque, New Mexico
Charges Description: Police tracked Dominguez to a Comfort Suites hotel after a prior SWAT standoff. During arrest attempt, Dominguez leapt from a window, was tackled by K-9 Rebel, and used the dog as a shield while pointing a loaded (but unfired) gun at officers. Officers opened fire, killing Dominguez and mortally wounding Rebel.
 Link of Articles: https://www.officer.com/on-the-street/k-9-equipment-services/video/55297758/bodycam-shows-deadly-hotel-clash-that-left-albuquerque-new-mexico-police-k-9-armed-suspect-dead
In Case of Missing BWC Footage:Should body-worn cameras not be utilized by your agency, kindly notify me so we can adjust accordingly. However, if this request involves a State Trooper, dashcam footage is still required.Exclusions & Redactions:I understand the importance of privacy and sensitivity. Please ensure the following:Any Personally Identifiable Information (PII) is redacted.Any minor or uninvolved party appearances are omitted.Graphic, explicit, or sensitive content is blurred, redacted, or removed.Any other legally necessary redactions are made at your discretion.Preferred Format:Please provide the responsive records in digital format, via a secure platform such as Evidence.com, iCrimeFighter, Box.com, or a similar secure delivery service
Thank you for your time and dedication to public transparency. If you have any questions or need additional information to fulfill this request, feel free to contact me. I look forward to your response. If physical delivery is necessary, I am happy to provide a mailing address upon request.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 15 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Hamna

communications.subject: Your City of Albuquerque public records request #25-14672 has been submitted.
communications.communication:
City of Albuquerque ************************************************************************ Your record request #25-14672 has been submitted successfully. Greetings: We have received your request for public records and will begin processing your request. This correspondence is intended to acknowledge your request and alert you that it may take up to fifteen days to process your request. NMSA 1978 14-2-8(D). We will be in contact with you as we process your request if we need additional information or if it appears that your request is excessively burdensome and broad. Please note, the City Clerk's Office receives 1,100-1,500 requests per month and we are currently working on approximately 3,000 requests for public records, including yours. Planning /Fire/Environmental Health Department Records: If you are requesting records from the Planning, Fire, or Environmental Health Departments, please make sure to review City of Albuquerque Info Connect. That website may provide you with the information you are seeking regarding current development projects and other matters. Police Department: Please be advised, if you are requesting lapel and/or 911 audio from the Albuquerque Police Department (APD), your request may take a significant amount of time to review and provide the records. In lieu of the 911 audio, my office can provide the Computer Aided Dispatch (CAD). The CAD provides information of when the call was received, when and what officers were dispatched, and a description of what happens throughout the incident. In addition, please keep in mind a 5 minute lapel video can take up to 20 minutes to review depending on the type of redactions that are necessary to complete. We will be in contact to discuss ways to narrow your request but you are also welcome to contact us to discuss narrowing options. If you have or later acquire documents relating to your request, please let us know and upload the records into NextRequest. Such additional information has proven to be a useful resource in identifying, locating, and producing additional records. We are unable to open any links whether unsolicited, unverified, or otherwise due to the high risk of phishing, malware, or other malicious redirections. Providing information through a link may prevent or delay us from reviewing any additional details you submit. Please do not hesitate to contact us if you would like to know the status of your request, and please communicate all questions and status updates via NextRequest. The Office of the City Clerk reserves the right to charge an advance/deposit fee for materials related to records production and data extraction.  You may access your request by signing into your NextRequest profile at the following website:  https://nextrequest.cabq.gov/users/sign_in  Sincerely, Ethan Watson City Clerk ************************************************************************ Reply to this email or sign in to contact City of Albuquerque.

City of Albuquerque ************************************************************************ A message was sent to you regarding record request #25-14672: Hello, Based on an initial review of your request, our office is asking that you narrow your request for public records. We are reaching out to you specifically because your request appears to have a significant amount of potentially non-exempt responsive lapel footage, which is the most time consuming record type for our office to process. For example, a 1-hour recording requires 3-4 hours to review and redact. In most cases, the first responding Officer’s lapel video contains the information most people are seeking. If you are able to narrow your request to that Officer’s lapel it can avoid tens to hundreds of hours of review and redaction (which results in additional time needed to respond to your request). It may also reduce the overall cost of your request. At this time, we project that the cost associated with this request will be in excess of ten ($10.00) dollars. Please review your request and let us know if there is a way you can narrow your request for records. If you decide not to narrow your request, we will conduct a reasonable search and process your request accordingly. If you are able to provide a subpoena for the records instead of an IPRA request please consider withdrawing your IPRA request and submitting a subpoena in lieu of the IPRA requests Sincerely, Michael Pruitt Asenap IPRA Intake Coordinator Office of the City Clerk ************************************************************************ Questions about your request? Yael

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: WNP-136 Emails (Frank Klotz)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

All emails sent to, from, or copied to Frank Klotz from January 1, 2014 to December 31, 2018 containing the non-case-sensitive key-string "WNP-136". After conducting a search to determine how many email records exist, if these records are too cumbersome to go through, please let me know the total number of records for the time period requested and I may desire to modify my request to limit the keywords or timeframe.

You may exclude emails that may be classified as newsletters, junk, or spam.

Please include attachments to the emails as well.

If any part of these documents are exempt from disclosure, please be sure to review and release all reasonably segregable nonexempt portions of responsive documents, as the FOIA requires.

I request that I be properly classified as a media requester. I am an investigative journalist who has written numerous articles on topics of public interest for the Asia Times, Responsible Statecraft, the National Interest, Reason Magazine, America Magazine and the Armenian Weekly, and I am requesting these documents in an editorial capacity. Please contact me if you have any questions about my media status.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Matthew Petti
